items.name: Honeycomb-Surfels: Compact Hexagonal Primitives for Efficient Scene Rendering and Reconstruction
items.title: Honeycomb-Surfels: Compact Hexagonal Primitives for Efficient Scene Rendering and Reconstruction
items.description: Novel view synthesis and 3D reconstruction have advanced rapidly with radiance fields and splatting, yet their memory and computational demands limit their use in resource-constrained settings. We introduce Hexels: novel planar hexagonal surface elements with a first-order spatial color field for efficient 3D scene and 2D image representation. items.title: ThinkWorld: World Imagination Reinforces Chain-of-Dynamics Reasoning
items.description: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have made substantial progress in robotic manipulation, but their generalization remains constrained by the diversity and coverage of action-labeled robot demonstrations. Human videos provide much broader behavioral and environmental experience, while learning from them faces a fundamental trade-off between scalable data and explicit action grounding. items.name: When Should We Intervene at Test Time?
items.title: When Should We Intervene at Test Time?
items.description: Test-time adaptation helps a deployed model respond to changing inputs, but the same intervention can rescue one batch and damage the next. Updating normalization statistics, for example, can improve corrupted images yet fail when a batch contains mostly one class. items.name: Heads of Security: Learned Attention Gates Improve Prompt Injection Robustness
items.title: Heads of Security: Learned Attention Gates Improve Prompt Injection Robustness
items.description: We introduce Heads of Security (HoS), a prompt injection defense that enforces instruction-data separation via a small set of learned per-head attention gates. HoS learns how each head should redistribute attention between trusted and untrusted tokens, enabling models to reason over untrusted content without following injected instructions. items.title: KPPax: preprocess differentiable kinetic ODE for machine learning in atmospheric chemistry
items.description: Atmospheric chemical mechanisms are commonly distributed in the language of the Kinetic PreProcessor (KPP), which generates efficient Fortran or C code but does not fit into the differentiable programming frameworks in which machine-learning models are developed. items.title: Pushing Dexterity and Safety for In-Hand Object Pose Reaching That Works Remarkably Well
items.description: Dexterous manipulation with multi-fingered hands is the next frontier of robotics, yet learned hand skills remain limited to simple grasps or basic repeated motions, such as rotating an object. As robots attempt more demanding in-hand maneuvers, safety, such as not dropping the object, becomes critical, yet it is rarely measured. items.name: GEPA-Curator: Curated Learning for Self Improving Agents
items.title: GEPA-Curator: Curated Learning for Self Improving Agents
items.description: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used in multi-turn agentic workloads that require sustained interaction with complex environments. Existing reflective prompt optimizers such as GEPA learn from failed rollouts, but agentic failures can also come from prompt weaknesses, harness limitations, stochastic execution, or noisy judges. items.name: Can LLMs Uncover Hidden Physical Laws through Free Exploration?
items.title: Can LLMs Uncover Hidden Physical Laws through Free Exploration?
items.description: Scientific discovery often begins with an unexpected observation that prompts a new research question. In a world with altered physical laws, can large language models (LLMs) notice unexpected behavior, such as heavier objects falling more slowly, and discover the law through experiments without being told what to investigate? items.title: Scaling Laws for Tool-Use Agents via Controllable Environment Synthesis
items.description: We explore how to build performant large language model (LLM) tool-use agents that complete complex, multi-step tasks. Specifically, we study how data composition in synthetically generated tool-use environments affects the training of such agents. items.title: MuonGS: Pretraining LLMs with Relaxed Weight-Norm Control

items.title: Multi-State Linear Attention with Generalized Second-Order Routing

items.title: Metacognitive Decoding: Efficient Inference for Diffusion Language Agents
items.description: Diffusion language models offer a promising path to efficient agents through parallel token generation. However, efficient interaction requires adapting both where computation is spent and how much text is generated. items.title: What Improves During Pretraining? Tracking Knowledge Acquisition with Point-in-Time Models
items.description: Language models pretrained on web corpora collected over multiple years learn both general and domain-specific knowledge. How these different kinds of knowledge are learned as pretraining progresses remains unclear. items.description: When an LLM group's discussion is compressed into a short memory for a final decision maker, what should the memory keep? Two natural heuristics keep the rarest claims or the claims relevant to the decision criteria. items.title: VideoLVR: Latent Visual Reasoning over Grounded Video Evidence
items.description: Chain-of-thought reasoning has substantially advanced video understanding in multimodal large language models (MLLMs). items.title: Beyond Answer Changes: Matched Same-Class Controls for Local Audio Evidence
items.description: For audio-language models, an answer change after a local sound-event edit can reflect a response to the event's class, sensitivity to waveform rewriting, or both. items.name: MoI-Bench: A Benchmark for Image Generation and Editing on Mobile Devices
items.title: MoI-Bench: A Benchmark for Image Generation and Editing on Mobile Devices
items.description: Developing on-device image models requires considering practical user needs, task types and device resource constraints. However, existing benchmarks provide limited guidance on identifying capability gaps between on-device models and server-side models. We introduce MoI-Bench, a benchmark grounded in mobile user needs, comprising 64 subtasks and 1150 samples. items.description: Traffic forecasting requires modeling complex temporal dynamics and the spatial dependencies imposed by road topology. items.description: World models are widely proposed as core components for enabling agents to reason over long temporal and spatial horizons. items.title: REGER: Modeling inter-item Relations with Semantic IDs for Generative Recommendation
items.description: Personalized recommendation depends on learning semantic and collaborative relations among items from online content and user interactions. items.title: Zero-Shot Multimodal Event Spotting in Soccer Broadcasts
items.description: Automatic soccer event spotting supports highlight generation, video indexing, and sports analytics, but existing methods depend on large annotated datasets and soccer-specific training. items.title: Spectral Braids: A Topological Descriptor for Dynamic Directed Networks
items.description: Eigenvalues are a workhorse of graph machine learning: spectral clustering, spectral graph neural networks, and graph kernels all summarize a network by the eigenvalues of a matrix. These eigenvalues are almost always treated as a static list of numbers. When a graph changes, however, its eigenvalues move, and when the matrix is not symmetric, they move in the complex plane, where they can wind around each other. items.title: TeamGym: A Gym for Team Decision-Making by AI Agents with Distributed Information
items.description: Many real-world decisions require teams to integrate information distributed across participants. Yet AI agents are still primarily trained and benchmarked in isolation. items.title: LCM-Promo: An LLM-Based Uplift Model for Promotion Allocation
items.description: We present LCM-Promo, an LLM-based uplift model for promotion allocation. items.title: Gym-Anything-RT: Scaling Real-Time Environments for Vision-Language Agents
items.description: AI agents have made substantial progress in domains where they have a non-trivial amount of time to deliberate between actions, such as mathematics, software engineering, and performing tasks on desktop applications. items.title: Pneuma: A Large-Scale Real-World Time Series Benchmark for Commercial Aircraft Predictive Maintenance
items.description: Predictive maintenance is vital for commercial aviation, yet progress remains hindered by the lack of public, large-scale real-world datasets. As a result, most methods are developed and evaluated on proprietary data, limiting reproducibility.
